children: on Thursday announced Canadian approval for an off-patent version of Novo’s
popular GLP-1 therapy, Ozempic, and a licensing deal with mAbxience, a company majority owned by Fresenius
Health Canada granted marketing authorization for its generic version of semaglutide, which Novo
markets as Ozempic for diabetes, the company said in a statement.

In Canada, diabetes is expected to impact nearly 7.3M people by 2034, up from approximately 6M currently, and the country’s GLP-1 market is worth an estimated $2.6B, with nearly 12M semaglutide injections used annually.
reaffirmed its 2026 outlook, ruling out any material financial contribution this year from potential launches of generic semaglutide.
Concurrently, the company announced a co-development and commercialization agreement for a biosimilar for emicizumab, which Roche
markets as Hemlibra for hemophilia A in a global market worth roughly $5.7B.

title: Sandoz wins Canada nod for generic Ozempic; inks licensing deal for generic Hemlibra
